headline: JPMorgan chief Jamie Dimon says AI will cost some jobs and that the change must be phased in.
score_reason: Pool 7 lowered by 2: old Davos remarks from January 2026 re-dated on 7 Oct with no new facts.
importance_line: Dimon's warning on the speed of AI job change affects workers first and then banks planning staff, but his figures were hypothetical and the remarks are months old.
summary: Benzinga reports, in a piece also carried by Yahoo Finance, that Jamie Dimon, chief executive of JPMorgan Chase, said at the World Economic Forum in Davos in January 2026 that AI will eliminate some jobs and change others, and that the speed of change matters. He used a hypothetical in which 2 million US truck drivers move from about $150,000 a year to jobs that might pay about $25,000, and said that would cause civil unrest, so the change should be phased in.
freshness: FOLLOW-UP of Jan 2026 (Davos remarks; exact day not stated)
